clue.text: Intellectual greeting on the radio, before b_____ argument

indicators.note: something heard over the airwaves is only heard, so the greeting word is taken by its sound

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
a censored expletive printed with only its first letter showing, so it gives just that letter
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A clever person shouts hello over the airwaves before a heated, expletive-laden quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The blanked-out word stands for a swear word printed as b_____, a polite newspaper convention; only its initial survives into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with lofty cultural or academic tastes is described by this term, a synonym for intellectual.

clue.text: Welcome sight in desert islands — reptile circling rivers

indicators.note: the word circling says the outer letters go round the inner ones

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, and plural islands gives two of them
R is the abbreviation for river, doubled for the plural
gator is the informal short form of alligator

explanation.surface: On desert islands, a crocodile-like creature lurks among the waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert islands' looks like one phrase, but 'desert' belongs to the definition and 'islands' gives two letter Is.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that waters arid ground would be a most welcome sight to anyone in a dry wasteland.

clue.text: Cat roaming in this place will cover quite an area

indicators.note: the word in places the scrambled letters within the other piece

parts.note: here means this place

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters of the word cat wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wandering cat will cover a lot of ground around here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaming' gives ECTA, which 'in' places inside; 'will cover' only links to the definition, which is the unit itself rather than a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This metric unit of land measures ten thousand square metres, which is quite a sizeable area.

clue.text: Going on, ignoring Football Association's call

indicators.note: ignoring says to leave out the named letters from the longer word

parts.note: faring means getting on or progressing, as in how are you faring
FA is the abbreviation for the Football Association, English football's governing body

explanation.surface: A football organisation carries on while overlooking a summons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes FA from FARING.
explanation.definitionFit: To telephone someone is to give them a call, which is a synonym in British usage.

clue.text: I hope for good things, successfully beginning to work with revitalised shire

parts.note: well means successfully, as in it went well

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the next word
revitalised means given new life, so the letters of shire are remade in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A hopeful local announces that a regenerated county is off to a good start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revitalised' makes ISHER from SHIRE. The definition is the answer speaking for itself in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who wants success and happiness for others voices exactly that sentiment: hoping things turn out fine.

clue.text: Boss cut reverie short

indicators.note: cut says a piece is removed from the reverie word, the piece being what makes it fall short

parts.note: a study, as in a brown study, is a state of deep thought or reverie
short, completing the split phrase cut short, names the final letter as the part to lop off

explanation.surface: The manager abruptly interrupted someone's daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut ... short' is one idea split round its object; 'short' drops the last letter. A brown study is an old phrase for a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss can be a raised ornamental knob, and a stud is a similar round projecting fastener or knob.

clue.text: Pondering bumping off family in obsession

indicators.note: bumping off is slang for killing, so a part of the word is done away with

parts.note: thinking means pondering
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Thinking about murdering one's relatives has become a fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' removes KIN from THINKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is an informal idiom for a fixation or preoccupation.

clue.text: Red and yellow would cover it (amongst many others)

definitions.text: Red and yellow would cover it (amongst many others)

indicators.note: words that cover something conceal it, so the letters sit inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Red and yellow are just two of many colours a single term would encompass.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'anD YEllow', and the whole clue also describes the answer: red and yellow are among many colourings it covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Red and yellow are examples of colouring agents, and the general term for such a colouring covers many others too.

clue.text: Soldiers turned up in most of film escapade

indicators.note: the word in places the reversed letters within the shortened film word
most of means all but the final letter

parts.note: a flick is informal for a film

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops appear in most of a movie about a daring adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' gives FLIC, 'turned up' suits a down entry read upwards, and 'in' places the soldiers inside. OR (other ranks) is a standard crossword term for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful lark or prank is a synonym for an escapade, both meaning a light-hearted spree.

clue.text: Biscuit? Opening new line, start to enjoy tucking in

indicators.note: tucking in means putting something inside, here the opening letter going into the other pieces

parts.note: a crack is a narrow opening

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone opens a fresh packet of biscuits and begins enjoying tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking in' sounds like eating, but it puts E inside CRACK + N + L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracknel is a light crisp kind of biscuit, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: 4 18 1 one girl had reviewed, dismissing alto

indicators.note: reviewed means looked at again, so the letters are viewed anew in a different order
dismissing means sending away, so the letter for alto is removed from the scrambled pool

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for alto in music

explanation.surface: A girl has gone over an opera without its alto part.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 and 18 are the answers RING and CYCLE, so the definition is part 1 of Wagner's Ring Cycle. 'reviewed' rearranges ONE GIRL HAD less the A that 'dismissing' takes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Das Rheingold is the opening opera of Wagner's four-opera cycle about the Nibelung ring.

clue.text: Wretched book soon to appear?

parts.note: looming means about to happen or emerge

explanation.surface: A miserable novel is about to be published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wretched' is the definition in its sense of a mild curse word, not 'miserable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooming is a British euphemism used as a mild intensifier like 'damned', matching wretched as an exasperated adjective.

clue.text: Congested situation? Preserve record first

indicators.note: first says this piece comes before the other

parts.note: a log is a written record
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A query about traffic leads to advice to keep a written record beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' reverses the clue's order of pieces: the record comes first in the answer although 'Preserve' is read first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile-up of floating timber blocking a river is the literal sense; figuratively it is any blockage or deadlock.

clue.text: 4 18 4 in vampire film with ghost foe active around day

parts.note: Twilight is the 2008 film about a teenage girl and a vampire

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go round the letter for day
active means busy and moving, so the letters of ghost foe are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: In a vampire movie, a spectral enemy prowls about by daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 18 4 means the fourth part of the RING CYCLE. 'active' rearranges GHOST FOE, and 'around' wraps it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Götterdämmerung, English title Twilight of the Gods, is the fourth and final opera in Wagner's Ring.

clue.text: Stop following transactions popular on social media

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the other

parts.note: TR is an abbreviation for transactions, as in learned society proceedings
an ending is a stop or conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone stops tracking deals that are popular online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop following' reads like unfollowing an account online, but 'Stop' is a noun meaning a conclusion and 'following' places it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic that is currently attracting a surge of posts and attention online is said to be doing this.

clue.text: Vague insurance for upholstery item

parts.note: loose means imprecise or vague
cover is the protection an insurance policy gives

explanation.surface: An imprecise insurance policy covers the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A removable fitted fabric casing for a sofa or armchair is an item of soft furnishing.

clue.text: See 14
Start and end of crappy clue not top-class? It gets repeated periodically

indicators.note: start and end of picks the first and last letters of the next word
not says the letter that follows is to be left out

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper class, top-class people or things

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating setter admits a clue is rubbish and not first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes U from CLUE, leaving CLE. U for upper class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of events that recurs in the same order over and over, like the seasons, is a recurring sequence.

clue.text: Cold, like a stream, freezing usual movement?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a stream ripples, so rippling describes running water

explanation.surface: An icy brook freezes in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: something that disables stops a person moving normally, as if frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disabling severely impairs ordinary motion, which is what freezing usual movement describes.

clue.text: I'd hazard ditching King for Welshman

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so a letter is thrown out

parts.note: a risk is a hazard
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Someone would chance abandoning a monarch in favour of a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' takes K from RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris is a traditional Welsh given name, as in the giant Idris of Cadair Idris, so it fits a man from Wales.

clue.text: Weak character's quiet tear about male

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a rip is a tear

explanation.surface: A feeble man quietly rips into the man in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A small or puny person is mocked with this word, likening them to a tiny crustacean.

clue.text: 4 18 3 soprano that is good and hot?

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
fried describes something cooked in hot fat, or a person overheated in the sun

explanation.surface: A query whether the soprano is both talented and overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 18 3 is the third opera of the RING CYCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried is the third opera in Wagner's four-part Ring, named after its hero.

clue.text: Member of fictional family, say, lacking heart, but surrounded by strength

indicators.note: surrounded by says the shortened word sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a forte is a strong point or strength

indicators.note: lacking heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A character from a novel family is spiritless yet hemmed in by power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking heart' leaves SY, and 'surrounded by' puts it inside the strength word. Galsworthy's saga is a classic of English fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forsytes are the wealthy clan in John Galsworthy's novel sequence The Forsyte Saga.

clue.text: Trivial mechanism's little good — I'm about to strain

parts.note: G is the short form of good
C is the abbreviation for circa, about
to rack is to strain or stretch, as on the rack

explanation.surface: A minor device is of little use, and someone is about to force it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimcrack is a showy but flimsy trinket or gadget, so a trivial contraption.

clue.text: Man having no time for practical lesson

indicators.note: having no says that letter is missing from the word

parts.note: a mortal is a human, man as opposed to god

explanation.surface: A busy fellow without a moment to spare wants hands-on instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' drops T from MORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The lesson drawn from a fable or experience about how to behave is called this.

clue.text: Avoid using one name in visit

parts.note: to drop something, as a player from a team, is to stop using it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Advice to skip a name when calling on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To call round on someone informally and briefly is the phrasal verb meaning visit.

clue.text: Work to bring in a drama

indicators.note: to bring in means to admit something inside, so the letter is placed within

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: A writer works to introduce a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece written for performance on stage is a common synonym for a drama.

clue.text: Discussion area supporting … I've forgotten what

parts.note: for means in favour of or supporting
um is the hesitant noise made when one cannot recall something

explanation.surface: A speaker trails off mid-sentence while backing some forgotten cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing-off is a performance of the hesitation sound itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A public meeting place or online board for debate is a place for discussion, from the Roman marketplace.

clue.text: Obscure lake avoided by hawk?

indicators.note: avoided by says the letter is kept out of the other word

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them, which is to flog them in British slang

explanation.surface: A bird of prey keeps clear of a remote lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning sell; FLOG is British slang for sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud or blur something is to obscure it, the verb sense of a misty murk.

clue.text: 4 18 2 curtailed farewell to Catholic prayer

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
the Kyrie, Lord have mercy, is a prayer in the Catholic Mass

explanation.surface: A shortened goodbye is said before a church prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 18 2 is the second opera of the RING CYCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Walküre, The Valkyrie, is the second opera of Wagner's Ring, named after Odin's warrior maidens.

clue.text: See 11
Essex town having year besieged by Elizabethan adventurer

indicators.note: besieged by means surrounded by, so the letter sits inside the name

parts.note: Sir Walter Raleigh was an explorer at the court of Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A town in Essex spends a year under siege by a Tudor explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London; Rayleigh is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayleigh is a market town in the south-east English county of Essex, an example of a town there.
